definition.def: If someone is your subordinate, they have a less important position than you in the organization that you both work for.
examples: Haig tended not to seek guidance from subordinates.
Nearly all her subordinates adored her.

definition.def: Someone who is subordinate to you has a less important position than you and has to obey you.
examples: Sixty of his subordinate officers followed his example.
Some people still regard women as subordinate to men. [+ to]

definition.def: Something that is subordinate to something else is less important than the other thing.
examples: It was an art in which words were subordinate to images. [+ to]

definition.def: If you subordinate something to another thing, you regard it or treat it as less important than the other thing.
examples: He was both willing and able to subordinate all else to this aim. [VERB noun + to]

examples.sentence: Indeed, if you wish to change your roles you must find some outward sign that you are doing so or you won't be permitted to change - the subordinate will continue to hear you as his boss no matter how hard you try to be his friend.
The subordinate females produce milk for the pups and take care of them in their underground burrows during the first three weeks of life.
